title: Microsoft Teams: events registration capacity rises to 20,000
summary: The registration limits, planned rollout, licensing and all eight control surfaces are supported. Minor corrections should clarify the existing policy documentation, cite the organiser-capacity guidance and keep the change log's December date provisional.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans support for up to 20,000 registrations for organisers with valid attendee packs.
claims.quote: Connect with more attendees than ever before with Teams Events, now supporting up to 20,000 registrations for organizers with valid Attendee packs.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The registration change affects Teams town halls and webinars using registration and their policy and licence administrators.
claims.quote: Organizers of Teams town halls and webinars that use registration- Admins who manage Teams events policies and Attendee Capacity Pack licenses

claims.claim: Registration capacity scales with the event's attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.
claims.quote: Starting in December, registration capacity for Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars scales with the event's attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams Enterprise organisers can allow up to 3,000 registrations without a capacity pack.
claims.quote: Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations.

claims.claim: Organisers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000 registrations.
claims.quote: Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Organisers needing more than 3,000 registrations need an Attendee Capacity Pack of the right size.
claims.quote: Make sure organizers who need more than 3,000 registrations per event have an Attendee Capacity Pack of the right size.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to begin rollout in early December 2026.
claims.quote: We will begin rolling out in early December 2026

claims.claim: Microsoft expects rollout to complete by late December 2026.
claims.quote: expect to complete by late December 2026.

claims.claim: The notice describes a Worldwide General Availability rollout.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide)

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft requires no administrator action for the change to arrive.
claims.quote: No action is required. To prepare, you can:

claims.claim: The new capacity is on upon rollout without an administrator enabling it.
claims.quote: Registration capacity scales with attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event. ... No action is required.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Large webinars with registration do not support broadcast-style streaming.
claims.quote: Large webinars with registration don't support broadcast-style streaming, which is available with town halls.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Broadcast-style streaming is available with town halls.
claims.quote: Large webinars with registration don't support broadcast-style streaming, which is available with town halls.

claims.claim: Organisers still need the right events policy.
claims.quote: Organizers still need the right events policy.

claims.claim: No new policy access is needed, only the right capacity pack where applicable.
claims.quote: No new policy access is needed, only the right Attendee Capacity Pack where applicable.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[2].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing Teams events policies and admin controls do not change.
claims.quote: Existing Teams events policies and admin controls don't change.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support more registrations in future releases.
claims.quote: We plan to support more registrations per event in future releases.

claims.claim: The cited feature comparison still lists registration as available up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: | [Registration](manage-registration-form-events) | Up to 1,000 attendees |

claims.claim: The notice recommends updating training and documentation mentioning a 1,000-registration limit.
claims.quote: Update internal training and documentation that mention a 1,000-registration limit.

claims.claim: The notice identifies no compliance considerations.
claims.quote: No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

claims.claim: No change to the feature's data access or destinations is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events registration capacity scheduling organizer registration maximum capacity data autonomous. Read MC1557760, the pack and comparison pages, and Plan for Teams events; none describes new data access or destinations for this capacity increase.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described for the registration-capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events registration capacity scheduling organizer registration maximum capacity data autonomous. Read MC1557760, the pack page and Plan for Teams events; these describe organiser-configured events, not autonomous actions from this capacity increase.

claims.claim: The organiser sets event capacity when scheduling the event.
claims.quote: Organizers use a unified creation flow to configure event settings—such as registration and attendee interaction—based on event capacity and scenario, rather than selecting a fixed event type.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/plan-events for the organiser's scheduling experience; the already cited pack page also states that an attendee pack determines the maximum capacity an organiser can set.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Removing a pack after scheduling can make upcoming events ineligible for their originally scheduled capacity.
claims.quote: If an attendee pack is removed after an event is scheduled, the upcoming event might no longer be eligible to run at the originally scheduled capacity.

claims.claim: Teams notifies both the admin and organiser when a pack removal threatens upcoming events.
claims.quote: To reduce the risk of event disruption, Teams notifies both the admin and the organizer.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licences for Teams Enterprise for events beyond the 3,000-attendee engagement capacity.
claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise that let event organizers host events for up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Pack sizes are 5K, 10K, 20K, 35K, 50K, 75K and 100K.
claims.quote: They can be purchased to support 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 event attendees.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: How packs combine
claims.claim: Teams Enterprise and pack capacities do not combine; a 20,000 pack gives 20,000, not 23,000.
claims.quote: The attendee capacities included with Teams Enterprise and an attendee pack aren't combined. For example, an organizer with a 20,000 attendee pack license can host events with engagement capabilities for up to 20,000 attendees (not 23,000).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each organiser can be assigned only one capacity pack at a time.
claims.quote: Each organizer can only be assigned one attendee pack at a time.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Learn pack pages publish no pack price at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack pricing price registration 3000 20000 charge. Opened attendee-capacity-pack and attendee-capacity-pack-manage in full; read events-licensing and eCDN purchasing/FAQ search excerpts. No pack price appears on the two pack pages.

claims.claim: A registration-specific charge is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack pricing price registration 3000 20000 charge. Read both pack pages, the comparison and assignment pages, MC1557760, and events-licensing and eCDN pricing search excerpts; no separate registration charge was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; front matter: cost
claims.claim: Mixed licensing and medium cost describe the Teams Enterprise baseline plus organiser add-on packs for the higher registration capacity.
claims.quote: Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations. Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000.

claims.claim: The Global Administrator role is required to manage licensing in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Teams Administrators have read-only access to the License Management section.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Pack assignment is at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Assign Add-on licenses > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. ... On the Licenses tab, select Assign to new users ... In the Assign Add-on licenses pane ... select the pack size that you want to assign in the Attendee pack column.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph can assign a purchased pack licence with POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request uses addLicenses containing assignedLicense objects with skuId.
claims.quote: addLicenses ... A collection of assignedLicense objects that specify the licenses to add. ... "addLicenses": [ { "disabledPlans": [], "skuId": "f30db892-07e9-47e9-837c-80727f46fd3d" } ]

claims.claim: removeLicenses identifies the licences to remove.
claims.quote: removeLicenses ... A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: Creation of events up to 1,000 attendees is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled allows events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled
claims.fix: Add one note covering the three events-policy commands: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference still labels the policy preview, although the management guide presents these controls without that label.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps, whose search excerpt states 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.'

claims.claim: The row correctly records the existing webinar control but qualifies its applicability above 1,000 attendees as unstated.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars. ... For events with more than 1,000 attendees, Optimize for large audience is on and can't be turned off.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].note with 'Existing control. Learn documents AllowWebinars for events with up to 1,000 attendees and AllowTownhalls for events optimised for large audiences.' The documentation describes the general policy reach; keep the separate question about the newly announced large webinars with registration.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Creation of large-audience events is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled allows large-audience events.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Town hall attendance is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone allows any user to attend large-audience events under the policy.
claims.quote: To allow any user to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone

claims.claim: EventAccessType is the corresponding attendance setting for events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, use the -EventAccessType parameter.

claims.claim: The Teams Events page shows purchased pack inventory and current assignments.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Teams Events page, you see your organization’s attendee pack inventory, including available attendee packs that you purchased and current assignments.

claims.claim: Admins can review an event inventory before removing or changing a pack.
claims.quote: You can view your attendee pack inventory, assign and manage licenses, and view your event inventory to monitor how attendee packs are used across your organization.

claims.claim: The first change note says registration capacity rises to 20,000 from December 2026 without labelling the date a plan.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.
claims.fix: Replace changes[0].note with 'First briefing: registration capacity for Teams webinars and town halls is planned to rise to 20,000 during December 2026, with the Attendee Capacity Pack needed above 3,000.'

claims.claim: The published material does not give a separate explicit registration-limit breakdown for each pack size below 20K.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams registration capacity Attendee Capacity Packs 5000 10000 registrations scales attendee capacity 20000. Read MC1557760 and pack, comparison and licensing pages/excerpts. MC states general scaling; no separate 5K/10K registration-limit table was found.
